thread:
Alex: Hey folks — I pushed the follow-up for the async-batching refactor (fixes and tests). I addressed the race condition Kahn pointed out and added a focused unit that reproduces the issue. Re-requesting a quick pass when you have time: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/2783
CI Bot: CI queued — running unit tests and linters (3/5 jobs started)
Priya: On my list today, will carve out 30m. quick q: do we preserve the old short-seq code path by default?
Alex: Yes — kept it behind a flag `legacy_short_seq` (default false). Added a short note in CHANGELOG and a comment above the conditional. snippet: `if short_seq and legacy_short_seq: return legacy_path()`
Sam: Skimming now. Left one nit about the `buffer_mgr` var name and a minor test fixture cleanup suggestion.
Jordan: Re: CI — I saw one GPU-only flake yesterday, might be unrelated but worth rerunning GPU job.
CI Bot: CI update: 4/5 jobs passed, gpu-integration rerun queued
Priya: Sounds good. If Alex's flag keeps behavior opt-in, I'm fine with merge after Sam's nit is addressed.
Sam: Updated the var name suggestion in a followup commit (split out small rename). PTAL — I can re-approve once green.
CI Bot: All checks passed — mergeable
Priya: LGTM after Sam's re-approve.
Sam: Re-approved. No blockers from my side.
Alex: Thanks! Planning to schedule canary deploy at 10:30 PT today. Will tag eng-oncall.
Jordan: I can watch the canary. Ping me ~10m beforehand and I'll stand by.
Alex: Will do, thanks :thumbsup: :party_parrot:
Jordan: Also, note for follow-up: add perf benchmark in next PR, there was a small 2% throughput dip on long sequences.
Alex: Noted — creating a backlog ticket for perf investigation.
